items.t: The page is headed "Mission West Homes for Sale | Acreages & View Properties," with a live feed that showed 53 results ("1-12 / 53") at reading — a snapshot, not a market statistic. Its editorial heading is "Mission West: Scenic and Established," describing hillside living, panoramic views and newer homes (site copy, not verified fact).

Feed scope — the identity call: every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Mission-West" with a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Wilson Street, Hayward Street, Olson Avenue, Haffner Terrace, Silverdale Avenue, Keystone Avenue, Gunn Avenue, Nelson Street and Townshipline Avenue. The page covers the western side of the City of Mission — the Silverdale area and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin — and this ground IS inside the City, so City planning, zoning and tax rules are the relevant municipal frame.

Sub-area context, labelled as context only (dwellings, NOT land): Mission West, September 2026 — Detached 5 / 1 / 20%; Condos & Townhomes 8 / 0 / NA. Community context (NOT Mission West figures): Mission Detached median $814,000; Condos & Townhomes median $430,000, September 2026. No sub-area median is published for Mission West: Not verified.

Transit and hospital anchors: West Coast Express — five weekday westbound trains from Mission City Station at 5:25–7:25 a.m. reach Waterfront Station in 75 minutes, five eastbound returns, no weekend or holiday service; Mission West is the far side of the city from the station and station-to-door times for any Mission West address are not verified — and Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, on the eastern/central side of the city from Mission West.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mission West

items.t: City plan: Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted April 21, 2026: Zoning is Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020. A specific parcel's zone and designation: confirm with the City for the PID.

Silverdale frame: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in the OCP and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway. Development timing, densities and population claims for individual listings are listing copy only: Not verified for any specific parcel.

Rural frame inside the city: the City's Rural Mission Strategy covers the City's rural communities — "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods" — building on the new OCP. Rural character here does not mean FVRD government: Stave Falls and Steelhead are inside the City of Mission.

SSMUH / suites (City frame): Secondary suites: all suites must be registered with the City; a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; a new suite goes through the building permit process; an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus applicable utility user fees applies. The in-house suite size cap, any owner-occupancy rule, and the Zoning Bylaw Section 109 parking count for Mission: Not verified.

Strata block (for Archer Green-type built strata, and for a bare-land strata lot wherever one trades — none is verified on this ground): Form B (SPA s.59) within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page, with rules, budget and most recent depreciation report attached; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022 (short-term may still be restricted); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + Reg 7.01 + May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

City property taxes — FLAT 10% penalty: City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss.233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s.3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s.235). The rural 5% + 5% regime does NOT apply to any Mission West parcel.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission West

items.t: Mission West publishes no price of its own. The land itself has no published statistic at all.

Silverdale's growth story is real; a parcel's share of it is not yet written. The 3,440-acre SCPA designation, the Central Neighbourhood Plan and the Master Infrastructure Strategy are City-documented and underway — but no density, timing or servicing promise for an individual parcel is verified until it is read off that parcel's designation, zoning and the DSCB 5650-2017 process.

The Wilson Street parks carry two board labels. The same park addresses are labelled "Mission-West" on this feed and "Stave Falls" on the stave-falls feed — not verified as a board-boundary question; the label changes neither tenure (pad rent under the MHPTA) nor the City tax frame.

The far side of the city is far from its anchors. Mission City Station and Mission Memorial Hospital (7324 Hurd Street) both sit on the eastern/central side — a Mission West acreage buyer pricing a "75-minute West Coast Express commute" is pricing station-to-Waterfront time only; station-to-door time for any Mission West address is not verified.

items.t: "Mission West" is an MLS® sub-area name for the western side of the City of Mission — the Silverdale area and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin. The guide feed sits inline with a count header "1-12 / 53" (snapshot only), headed "Mission West Homes for Sale | Acreages & View Properties", and every first-page card read is labelled Mission-West, Mission, Status: Active, on Silverdale Avenue, Keystone Avenue, Nelson Street, Gunn Avenue, Wilson Road/Street and Townshipline Avenue. Read gap: the guide page's tail (lines ~829–1184) could not be read pass (fetch-service 429, stopped rather than retried); content in that stretch is not verified.
Combined Mission community — Detached median $814,000; attached median $430,000, expressly NOT Mission West figures. No Mission West median is published: Not verified.

The defining plan area: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in Mission's Official Community Plan and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway. Development timing, densities and population claims for individual Silverdale listings in feed text are listing copy only: Not verified as facts for any specific parcel. The City's Rural Mission Strategy also covers this side of the city — "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods" — building on the new Official Community Plan.

SD75's structure is elementary K–6, middle 7–9, secondary 10–12. Catchments: Not verified for any Mission West address — no catchment lookup is on record; the guide page's catchment assertions are guide-only claims.

Transit: TransLink's West Coast Express timetable (effective January 5, 2026) runs five weekday trains westbound from Mission City Station at 5:25, 5:55, 6:25, 6:55 and 7:25 a.m., arriving Waterfront 75 minutes later, and five eastbound trains from Waterfront at 3:50, 4:20, 4:50, 5:30 and 6:20 p.m.; no weekend or statutory-holiday service. blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mission West

items.t: OCP — City of Mission Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted April 21, 2026: Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is IN PREPARATION, NOT adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026; no corridor-plan adoption is claimed for the Highway 7 corridor serving this side of the city.
Zoning — City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: Any Mission West parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, not verified.

Secondary suites — Mission: all secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a secondary suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; a new suite goes through the building permit process; and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus applicable utility user fees applies. The in-house suite size cap, any owner-occupancy rule, and the exact Section 109 parking stall count are not verified — not stated on the City pages read.

SSMUH — Mission: SSMUH incorporation is Bylaw 6299-2024 (July 17, 2024), verified via City sources; Mission has adopted the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation, subject to eligibility and servicing. Whether SSMUH unit counts apply to a given Mission West lot is per-parcel: Not confirmed — Mission unit counts for this ground remain not confirmed, and Surrey figures are never imported here.

Subdivision and servicing — Mission: Mission's Development and Subdivision Control Bylaw is 5650-2017 (DSCB 5650-2017 — stated from a City source found in an earlier pass; title confirmed on mission.ca; carried with that sourcing). Subdivision potential follows the parcel's zone minimums and, where ALR applies, ALC approval (ALR block below).

Property taxes — City of Mission (Mission West is city land, stated expressly): City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a FLAT 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss.233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s.3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s.235). The FVRD rural regime — Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, 5% after July 2 + 5% after October 31 — does NOT apply to a Mission West parcel; the two regimes are different and are never blended.

ALR block (applies where a Mission West parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). The guide page's at-a-glance cards note Fraser River edge ALR lands on this ground; no ALR parcel count or split is documented, and none is invented.
Pad tenure, where met (Wilson Street park homes in the feed): a manufactured home on a rented pad is NOT lot stock / NOT land ownership.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission West

items.t: Silverdale is a plan in process, not a finished suburb (City sources, read Nov 1, 2026). The 3,440-acre Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is designated for urban growth in the OCP, but its Central Neighbourhood Plan and Master Infrastructure Strategy are still underway — a Silverdale parcel's value story is a timing question the listing cannot answer; only the in-force designation and zoning for the PID can.
The 20% ratio is one sale (Sep 2026). Present it as a thin-market signal, never as proof Mission West is Mission's hottest market.

Guide-only claims (the Central Neighbourhood Plan map date, Stave Heights plan dates and setback figure, Centennial Park / Activity Hub and Tea House details, the Silverdale Urban Forest recommended designation, the Silverdale townhome rezoning example, the MLS median detached lot size, the 2011 Mission ALR inventory figure, and the SD75 catchment assertions) are not verified site copy, not defects and not facts.
